literal: Virtue-not-associating poverty, the mother who bore [him] even, like a stranger, to be looked at will happen.
translation: Even the mother who gave birth to him will look upon a man as a stranger, if he is afflicted by poverty that is devoid of virtue.
modern: அறநெறியோடு பொருந்தாத வறுமை உடையவனை, அவனைப் பெற்ற தாயும் கூட ஒரு அந்நியனைப் போலத் தான் பார்ப்பாள்.
explanation: This couplet illustrates the devastating social impact of poverty. The poet states that when a person is trapped in a miserable poverty that lacks any virtuous support or dignity, even their own mother will look at them coldly, as if they were a stranger. The term 'அறஞ்சாரா' (not aligned with virtue) suggests a state of destitution so severe that it strips away moral standing and social respect. By using the mother—the ultimate symbol of unconditional love—as the one who turns away, the verse emphasizes how poverty destroys even the strongest human bonds.
